title: Changing a suprapubic catheter

guidelineVersions: BAUS suprapubic catheter practice guidelines — revised (2020, BJU International)
BAUS Suprapubic catheter patient information leaflet F25/035 (January 2025)

brief.scenario: A 71-year-old with a long-term suprapubic catheter (placed 10 months ago) attends for a scheduled exchange. The existing catheter is draining clear urine.
brief.task: You are a core surgical trainee asked to demonstrate safe exchange on a task trainer and explain what you would do if insertion fails. Demonstrate the procedure on the model, explain decisions aloud and respond to examiner prompts. Do not perform a procedure on a real patient in this station.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: This is an established-tract exchange, not a new suprapubic catheter insertion.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Forcing replacement when resistance is met or losing the tract without urgent urological help.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: Confirm the date of first placement, indication, allergies, previous difficult exchanges, and that a trained operator and backup pathway are available.

flow: Confirm indication, maturity, consent and equipment
Check drainage and position; undertake aseptic preparation
Demonstrate controlled removal and prompt, gentle replacement on the trainer
Confirm urinary drainage and absence of pain/resistance before balloon inflation
Secure, document, advise and escalate immediately if replacement fails

grid.label: Identity, indication and mature tract
grid.pass: Confirms identity, established tract and date, consent and appropriateness
grid.high: Also anticipates previous difficult changes and individualised plan

grid.label: Infection and contraindication screen
grid.fail: Misses fever, pain or blocked catheter
grid.pass: Checks systemic symptoms, catheter drainage, pain and allergy
grid.high: Explains when to defer routine exchange and seek review

grid.label: Asepsis and preparation
grid.pass: Hand hygiene, aseptic field, correct replacement and balloon equipment
grid.high: Plans for immediate failed-change escalation before withdrawal

grid.label: Existing catheter inspection
grid.pass: Observes catheter and existing insertion depth, balloon volume per record/device
grid.high: Explains encrustation, blockage and safe handling

grid.label: Controlled removal
grid.pass: Completely deflates and gently removes without force
grid.high: Pauses on pain or resistance and obtains help

grid.label: Gentle replacement
grid.pass: Introduces appropriate catheter promptly, gently along tract; stops on resistance
grid.high: Maintains urgent escalation plan to prevent tract closure

grid.label: Confirm before inflation
grid.pass: Confirms urine return / appropriate placement as demonstrated before sterile-water balloon inflation
grid.high: States no inflation if pain, uncertain position or absent drainage

grid.label: Secure, monitor and document
grid.pass: Connects drainage, secures, records catheter, balloon, return and issues
grid.high: Explains signs of misplacement and appropriate immediate review

grid.label: Escalation and discharge advice
grid.fail: Repeated blind attempts in a failed exchange
grid.borderline: Calls for help only after multiple attempts
grid.pass: Stops on resistance/no drainage, calls urology urgently; gives red flags
grid.high: Explains tract closure, alternative bladder drainage under specialist direction

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Hello. I need to swap your tube today.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Yes. I do not need to ask when it was inserted.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: He mentions he has felt shivery and his lower abdomen has been sore since yesterday.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: That is not relevant to a routine change; I will carry on.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I have a spare catheter. I will skip the sterile setup to save time.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I will not look at how far in it sits or check the balloon volume; I will just take it out.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: The old catheter catches on removal.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I will push through because the hole may close.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I would inflate the balloon anyway.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: What if it still will not drain?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I would try several more times before contacting urology.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Suppose the exchange succeeds but there is steady fresh bleeding around the catheter.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I would leave it unsecured, skip the notes and send them home; the bleeding will stop by itself.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Hello. I am the core surgical trainee. Could I confirm your identity and explain the catheter exchange? When was your suprapubic catheter first inserted?

pass.speaker: patient
pass.text: Ten months ago. It is usually changed every three months.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: May I check the catheter record, allergies and obtain your consent?

pass.speaker: patient
pass.text: Yes. I am allergic to latex.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Has it been draining? Any fever, abdominal pain, cloudy urine, bleeding or problems with past changes?

pass.speaker: patient
pass.text: It is draining clearly. No fever or pain. Last exchange went smoothly.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I will use a latex-free replacement of the recorded size, sterile field, drainage system and prescribed balloon volume. I will ensure help is accessible before I remove the old tube.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: You see a patent catheter. The recorded balloon volume is 10 mL.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I will note the insertion depth and inspect the site, urine and balloon record.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Demonstrate removal on the trainer.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I completely deflate the balloon according to the device and remove gently without traction against resistance.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Demonstrate replacement.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I promptly insert the lubricated appropriate catheter gently through the existing tract, without force.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: The model now shows urine draining.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: That supports intravesical placement. I would confirm according to protocol, inflate the balloon with the specified volume of sterile water, then gently seat it without traction.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What next?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Attach drainage, secure the tube, ensure free flow, document catheter details, balloon volume, urine return and any difficulty.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What if the new tube meets resistance and there is no urine return?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Stop; do not force or inflate the balloon. Seek urgent urology help, as the tract can close quickly. Arrange alternative bladder drainage only as directed by the appropriate team.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I would explain to the patient to seek urgent help for no drainage, pain, bleeding, fever or a dislodged catheter.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Hello. I am the core surgical trainee. I will check whether a routine exchange is appropriate before touching the catheter. May I confirm your details and consent? When was it first placed, and who usually changes it?

high.speaker: patient
high.text: Ten months ago. A specialist nurse changes it every three months.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I will review the catheter passport for size, balloon volume, latex allergy and any difficult exchanges.

high.speaker: patient
high.text: I have a latex allergy. No difficult changes so far.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Any current fever, shivering, suprapubic pain, blocked drainage, bleeding or new confusion?

high.speaker: patient
high.text: None; urine is coming through normally.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I confirm this is an established tract. I prepare a latex-free same-size catheter, sterile supplies and closed drainage, and know how to summon urgent urology support if replacement fails.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: The tube is patent, the site clean; documentation records 10 mL in the balloon.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I inspect and note the external depth and look for encrustation, infection or granulation. I would avoid a routine exchange if the patient is systemically unwell without reassessment.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: After aseptic preparation, I deflate fully and remove the old catheter gently while protecting the tract. I stop if it is stuck rather than using traction.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: The new catheter follows the tract without resistance.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I replace promptly and gently. I would not probe blindly if the course were uncertain.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I verify drainage and absence of pain; only once intravesical placement is supported do I inflate with the recorded sterile-water volume. If I cannot confirm position, I do not inflate.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I check continuing urine flow, secure against traction and complete a catheter passport record including size, batch if required, volume, site condition and review date.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Unexpectedly, resistance develops during a future change and no urine returns.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I stop immediately and do not repeatedly reinsert, dilate or inflate. I urgently contact urology because the tract may close; assess retention, pain and observations while a senior agrees a safe drainage plan.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I would give clear advice about displacement, blockage, haematuria, fever and pain, with urgent contact details.

failures.move: Pulling a catheter with an inflated balloon

failures.consequence: Tissue injury and failed bladder drainage.

failures.move: Delay or repeated failed attempts without escalation

recovery.line: I cannot confirm placement, so I will not inflate the balloon; I am stopping and asking urology to assist urgently.

recovery.when: If you have not yet confirmed the catheter age and record
recovery.line: I have not yet confirmed the catheter age and record; I will do that before removing a working catheter.

knowledge.fact: The first change of a new suprapubic catheter is usually after six to 12 weeks, once the tract has matured; it is often done in hospital.
Long-term suprapubic catheters are normally changed every three months, or as the device and care plan specify.
If an SPC falls out, prompt specialist help is needed because the tract may close.
Stop on resistance or uncertain placement and avoid blind balloon inflation.
Treat symptomatic infection/cellulitis rather than asymptomatic colonisation.
Document catheter size, balloon volume, placement confirmation and subsequent drainage.

recall.think: Established tract, working catheter and a plan for failed exchange.
recall.say: “I will not force the tube or inflate a balloon in an uncertain position.”
do: Asepsis, deflate completely, gentle replacement, confirm drainage, then inflate.

numbers.meaning: First change usually 6–12 weeks after insertion

recall.trap: Tract loss after repeated blind attempts when reinsertion fails.
recall.finish: Secure, observe flow, document and provide urgent-return advice.

partner.opening: Demonstrate the procedure on the model, explain decisions aloud and respond to examiner prompts.
partner.actorBrief: Patient: calm 71-year-old; reveal first placement 10 months ago only when asked. Latex allergy and uneventful prior exchanges only on direct questions.

reveals.finding: patent clear-draining tube and 10 mL recorded balloon

curveballs.safeAnswer: candidate should stop and urgently escalate.

curveballs.prompt: no urine return before balloon inflation
